intro: A command palette gives people a keyboard-first way to search and run actions from anywhere in an app. Zentauri UI ships a composable Command primitive with a global Cmd+K hotkey, grouped results, live filtering, an empty state, and an optional animated entry — themeable through --zui-command-* tokens.
useCases: Global Cmd+K navigation across pages and resources.
Quick action launchers in dashboards and developer tools.
Searchable menus that combine navigation and commands.

faqs.question: Does Command support a global Cmd+K shortcut?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set the hotkey prop (defaults to k) and the palette binds meta/ctrl + key to toggle open from anywhere.

faqs.question: How does keyboard navigation work?
faqs.answer: Arrow Up and Down move the active item, Enter selects it and fires onSelect, and Escape closes the palette. Typing filters items by value and keywords.

faqs.question: Is there an animated command palette?
faqs.answer: Yes. Import CommandContentAnimated from the animated entrypoint to spring the palette in; it falls back to a fade when reduced motion is preferred.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body:
Render a portal dialog with a search input, grouped items, separators, and an empty state.

Filtering, active-item tracking, and keyboard navigation are handled internally.

sections.heading: Composition and API
sections.body: Compose Command with CommandTrigger, CommandContent, CommandInput, CommandList, CommandGroup, CommandItem, CommandSeparator, CommandEmpty, and CommandFooter. Use appearance and size variants for visual tone, and the hotkey prop for a global shortcut.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: The palette renders role=dialog with aria-modal, traps focus while open, restores focus on close, and exposes the input as a combobox with role=option items. Provide a label for the dialog.

sections.heading: Next.js integration notes
sections.body: Use Command inside client components since it manages open state and key handlers in the browser. The base entry stays free of framer-motion; import CommandContentAnimated only where you want motion.
